stem: Write pseudocode for a function `Partition(Low, High)` that uses `Data[High]` as the pivot, moves the smaller items before it and returns the final position of the pivot. [4]

points.description: Sets the pivot to Data[High] and a boundary to Low
A loop from Low to High - 1 comparing each item with the pivot
Swaps an item smaller than the pivot with the item at the boundary and adds 1 to the boundary
After the loop swaps the pivot into the boundary position and returns the boundary

answerSpec.markingNotes:
Example answer: ```
FUNCTION Partition(Low : INTEGER, High : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER
    DECLARE Pivot, Boundary, Index, Temp : INTEGER
    Pivot ← Data[High]
    Boundary ← Low
    FOR Index ← Low TO High - 1
        IF Data[Index] < Pivot THEN
            Temp ← Data[Index]
            Data[Index] ← Data[Boundary]
            Data[Boundary] ← Temp
            Boundary ← Boundary + 1
        ENDIF
    NEXT Index
    Temp ← Data[Boundary]
    Data[Boundary] ← Data[High]
    Data[High] ← Temp
    RETURN Boundary
ENDFUNCTION
```

explanation: A boundary marks where smaller items end.
hints: Use a boundary and swap smaller items to it.
